1.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 called to Mosheh, and spoke to him from the Tent of Appointment, saying,
1.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When anyone of you brings an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, you bring your offering of the livestock, of the herd or of the flock.
1.3: ‘If his offering is a burnt offering of the herd, let him bring a male, a perfect one. Let him bring it at the door of the Tent of Appointment, for his acceptance before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.4: ‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
1.5: ‘And he shall slaughter the bull before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And the sons of Aharon, the kohenim, shall bring the blood and sprinkle the blood all around on the altar which is at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
1.6: ‘And he shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.
1.7: ‘And the sons of Aharon the kohĕn shall put fire on the altar, and lay the wood in order on the fire.
1.8: ‘And the sons of Aharon, the kohenim, shall arrange the pieces, with the head and the fat on the wood which is on the fire on the altar.
1.9: ‘But its entrails and its legs he washes with water. And the kohĕn shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.10: ‘And if his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats as a burnt offering, let him bring a male, a perfect one.
1.11: ‘And he shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And the sons of Aharon, the kohenim, shall sprinkle its blood on the altar all around.
1.12: ‘And he shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its fat, and the kohĕn shall arrange them on the wood which is on the fire on the altar.
1.13: ‘But the entrails and the legs he washes with water. And the kohĕn shall bring it all and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.14: ‘And if the burnt offering of his offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is of birds, then he shall bring his offering of turtledoves or young pigeons.
1.15: ‘And the kohĕn shall bring it to the altar, and shall wring off its head, and burn it on the altar, and its blood shall be drained out at the side of the altar.
1.16: ‘And he shall remove its crop with its feathers and throw it beside the altar on the east side, into the place for ashes.
1.17: ‘And he shall split it at its wings, but not sever it. And the kohĕn shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

10.1: And Naḏaḇ and Aḇihu, the sons of Aharon, each took his fire holder and put fire in it, and put incense on it, and brought strange fire before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which He had not commanded them.
10.2: And fire came out from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and consumed them, and they died before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
10.3: Then Mosheh said to Aharon, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke, saying, ‘By those who come near Me let Me be qodesh! And before all the people let Me be esteemed!’ ” And Aharon was silent.
10.4: And Mosheh called to Misha’ĕl and to Eltsaphan, the sons of Uzzi’ĕl the uncle of Aharon, and said to them, “Come near, take your brothers from before the qodesh place out of the camp.”
10.5: So they came near and took them by their long shirts out of the camp, as Mosheh had said.
10.6: And Mosheh said to Aharon, and to El’azar and to Ithamar, his sons, “Do not unbind your heads nor tear your garments, lest you die, and wrath come upon all the people. But let your brothers, all the house of Yisra’ĕl, bewail the burning which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has kindled.
10.7: “And do not go out from the door of the Tent of Appointment, lest you die, for the anointing oil of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is upon you.” And they did according to the word of Mosheh.
10.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Aharon, saying,
10.9: “Do not drink wine or strong drink, you, nor your sons with you, when you go into the Tent of Appointment, lest you die - a Law forever throughout your generations,
10.10: so as to make a distinction between the qodesh and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean,
10.11: and to teach the children of Yisra’ĕl all the Laws which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken to them by the hand of Mosheh.”
10.12: And Mosheh spoke to Aharon, and to El’azar and Ithamar, his sons who were left, “Take the grain offering that is left over from the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and eat it without leaven beside the altar, for it is most qodesh.
10.13: “And you shall eat it in a qodesh place, because it is yours by law and your sons’ by law, of the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for so I have been commanded.
10.14: “And the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you eat in a clean place, you, and your sons, and your daughters with you. For they are yours by law and your sons’ by law, which are given from the slaughterings of peace offerings of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
10.15: “The thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering they bring with the offerings of fat made by fire, to bring as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And it shall be yours and your sons’ with you, as a Law forever, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded.”
10.16: And Mosheh diligently looked for the goat of the sin offering and saw it was burned up. And he was wroth with El’azar and Ithamar, the sons of Aharon who were left, saying,
10.17: “Why have you not eaten the sin offering in a qodesh place, since it is most qodesh, and He has given it to you to bear the wickedness of the congregation, to make atonement for them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
10.18: “See, its blood was not brought inside the qodesh place. You should have eaten it without fail in a qodesh place, as I have commanded.”
10.19: And Aharon said to Mosheh, “See, today they have brought their sin offering and their burnt offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and these have come upon me! If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
10.20: And when Mosheh heard that, it was good in his eyes.

11.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying to them,
11.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘These are the living creatures which you do eat among all the beasts that are on the earth:
11.3: ‘Whatever has a split hoof completely divided, chewing the cud, among the beasts, that you do eat.
11.4: ‘Only, these you do not eat among those that chew the cud or those that have a split hoof: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, it is unclean to you;
11.5: and the rabbit, because it chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, it is unclean to you;
11.6: and the hare, because it chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, it is unclean to you;
11.7: and the pig, though it has a split hoof, completely divided, yet does not chew the cud, it is unclean to you.
11.8: ‘Their flesh you do not eat, and their carcasses you do not touch. They are unclean to you.
11.9: ‘These you do eat of all that are in the waters: any one that has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas or in the rivers, that you do eat.
11.10: ‘But all that have not fins and scales in the seas and in the rivers, all that move in the waters or any living creature which is in the waters, they are an abomination to you.
11.11: ‘They are an abomination to you - of their flesh you do not eat, and their carcasses you abominate.
11.12: ‘All that have not fins or scales in the waters is an abomination to you.
11.13: ‘And these you do abominate among the birds, they are not eaten, they are an abomination: the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,
11.14: and the hawk, and the falcon after its kind,
11.16: and the ostrich, and the nighthawk, and the seagull, and the hawk after its kind,
11.17: and the little owl, and the fisher owl, and the great owl,
11.18: and the white owl, and the pelican, and the carrion vulture,
11.19: and the stork, the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.
11.20: ‘All flying insects that creep on all fours is an abomination to you.
11.21: ‘Only, these you do eat of every flying insect that creeps on all fours: those which have jointed legs above their feet with which to leap on the earth.
11.22: ‘These of them you do eat: the locust after its kind, and the destroying locust after its kind, and the cricket after its kind, and the grasshopper after its kind.
11.23: ‘But all other flying insects which have four feet is an abomination to you.
11.24: ‘And by these you are made unclean, anyone touching the carcass of any of them is unclean until evening,
11.25: and anyone picking up part of the carcass of any of them has to wash his garments, and shall be unclean until evening.
11.26: ‘Every beast that has a split hoof not completely divided, or does not chew the cud, is unclean to you. Anyone who touches their carcass is unclean.
11.27: ‘And whatever goes on its paws, among all the creatures that go on all fours, those are unclean to you. Anyone who touches their carcass is unclean until evening,
11.28: and he who picks up their carcass has to wash his garments, and shall be unclean until evening. They are unclean to you.
11.29: ‘And these are unclean to you among the creeping creatures that creep on the earth: the mole, and the mouse, and the tortoise after its kind,
11.30: and the gecko, and the land crocodile, and the sand reptile, and the sand lizard, and the chameleon.
11.31: ‘These are unclean to you among all that creep. Anyone who touches them when they are dead becomes unclean until evening.
11.32: ‘And whatever any of them in its dead state falls upon, becomes unclean, whether it is any wooden object or garment or skin or sack, any object in which work is done, it is put in water. And it shall be unclean until evening, then it shall be clean.
11.33: ‘Any earthen vessel into which any of them falls, whatever is in it becomes unclean, and you break it.
11.34: ‘Any of the food which might be eaten, on which water comes, becomes unclean, and any drink which might be drunk from it becomes unclean.
11.35: ‘And on whatever their carcass falls becomes unclean - an oven or cooking range - it is broken down. They are unclean, and are unclean to you.
11.36: ‘But a fountain or a well, a collection of water, is clean, but whatever touches their carcass is unclean.
11.37: ‘And when their carcass falls on any planting seed which is to be sown, it is clean.
11.38: ‘But when any water is put on the seed and any part of any such carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.
11.39: ‘And when any of the beasts which are yours for food dies, he who touches its carcass becomes unclean until evening.
11.40: ‘And he who eats of its carcass has to wash his garments, and shall be unclean until evening. And he who picks up its carcass has to wash his garments, and shall be unclean until evening.
11.41: ‘And every creeping creature that creeps on the earth is an abomination, it is not eaten.
11.42: ‘Whatever crawls on its stomach, and whatever goes on all fours, and whatever has many feet among all creeping creatures that creep on the earth, these you do not eat, for they are an abomination.
11.43: ‘Do not make yourselves abominable with any creeping creature that creeps, and do not make yourselves unclean with them, lest you be defiled by them.
11.44: ‘For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and you shall qadosh yourselves. And you shall be qodesh, for I am qodesh. And do not defile yourselves with any creeping creature that creeps on the earth.
11.45: ‘For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is bringing you up out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be your Elohim. And you shall be qodesh, for I am qodesh.
11.46: ‘This is the Torah of the beasts and the birds and every living creature that moves in the waters, and of every creature that creeps on the earth,
11.47: to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that is eaten and the living creature that is not eaten.’ ”

12.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
12.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘When a woman has conceived, and has given birth to a male child, then she shall be unclean seven days, as in the days of her monthly separation she is unclean.
12.3: ‘And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin is circumcised.
12.4: ‘And she remains in the blood of her cleansing thirty-three days. She does not touch whatever is qodesh, and she does not come into the Miqdash until the days of her cleansing are completed.
12.5: ‘But if she gives birth to a female child, then she shall be unclean for two weeks, as in her monthly separation, and she remains in the blood of her cleansing for sixty-six days.
12.6: ‘And when the days of her cleansing are completed, for a son or for a daughter, she brings to the kohĕn a lamb a year old, as a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering, to the door of the Tent of Appointment.
12.7: ‘And he shall bring it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood. This is the Torah for her who has given birth to a male or a female.
12.8: ‘And if she is not able to bring a lamb, then she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a burnt offering and the other as a sin offering. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.’ ”

13.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
13.2: “When a man has on the skin of his body a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot, and it shall become on the skin of his body like a leprous infection, then he shall be brought to Aharon the kohĕn or to one of his sons the kohenim.
13.3: “And the kohĕn shall look at the infection on the skin of the body. And if the hair on the infection has turned white, and the infection appears to be deeper than the skin of his body, it is a leprous infection. And the kohĕn shall look at him, and pronounce him unclean.
13.4: “But if the bright spot is white on the skin of his body, and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, then the kohĕn shall shut up the infected one seven days.
13.5: “And the kohĕn shall look at him on the seventh day and see, if the infection appears to be as it was, and the infection has not spread on the skin, then the kohĕn shall shut him up another seven days.
13.6: “And the kohĕn shall look at him again on the seventh day and see, if the infection has darkened, and the infection has not spread on the skin, then the kohĕn shall pronounce him clean. It is a scab, and he shall wash his garments and be clean.
13.7: “But if the scab spreads further over the skin, after he has been seen by the kohĕn for his cleansing, he shall be seen by the kohĕn again.
13.8: “And the kohĕn shall look and see, if the scab has spread on the skin, then the kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean, it is leprosy.
13.9: “When the infection of leprosy is on a man, then he shall be brought to the kohĕn.
13.10: “And the kohĕn shall look and see, if the swelling on the skin is white, and it has turned the hair white, and there is a spot of raw flesh in the swelling,
13.11: it is an old leprosy on the skin of his body, and the kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean. He does not shut him up, for he is unclean.
13.12: “And if leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and the leprosy shall cover all the skin of the infected one, from his head to his foot, wherever the kohĕn looks,
13.13: then the kohĕn shall look and see, if the leprosy has covered all his body, he shall pronounce the infected one clean. It has all turned white, he is clean.
13.14: “But the day raw flesh appears on him, he is unclean.
13.15: “And the kohĕn shall look at the raw flesh and pronounce him to be unclean - the raw flesh is unclean, it is leprosy.
13.16: “Or when the raw flesh changes and turns white again, he shall come to the kohĕn.
13.17: “And the kohĕn shall look at him and see, if the infection has turned white, then the kohĕn shall pronounce the infected one clean, he is clean.
13.18: “And when the body has a boil in the skin, and it is healed,
13.19: and in the place of the boil there comes a white swelling or a bright spot, reddish-white, then it shall be seen by the kohĕn.
13.20: “And the kohĕn shall look and see, if it appears deeper than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean, it is a leprous infection which has broken out of the boil.
13.21: “But if the kohĕn looks at it and sees no white hairs in it, and it is not deeper than the skin, but has faded, then the kohĕn shall shut him up seven days;
13.22: and if it has spread further over the skin, then the kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean, it is a leprous infection.
13.23: “But if the bright spot stays in its place, it has not spread, it is the scar of the boil, and the kohĕn shall pronounce him clean.
13.24: “Or when the body receives a burn on its skin by fire, and the raw flesh of the burn shall become a bright spot, reddish-white or white,
13.25: then the kohĕn shall look at it and see, if the hair of the bright spot has turned white, and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy broken out in the burn. And the kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean, it is a leprous infection.
13.26: “But if the kohĕn looks at it and sees there are no white hairs in the bright spot, and it is not deeper than the skin, but has faded, then the kohĕn shall shut him up seven days.
13.27: “And the kohĕn shall look at him on the seventh day. If it spreads further over the skin, then the kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean, it is a leprous infection.
13.28: “But if the bright spot stays in its place, and has not spread on the skin, but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn. And the kohĕn shall pronounce him clean, for it is the scar from the burn.
13.29: “And when a man, or a woman, has an infection on the head or in the beard,
13.30: then the kohĕn shall look at the infection and see, if it appears deeper than the skin, and there is thin yellow hair in it, then the kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean, it is an eruption, a leprosy of the head or beard.
13.31: “But when the kohĕn looks at the infection of the eruption and sees that it does not appear deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then the kohĕn shall shut up the infection of the eruption seven days.
13.32: “And on the seventh day the kohĕn shall look at the infection and see, if the eruption has not spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the eruption does not appear deeper than the skin,
13.33: then he shall shave himself, but the eruption he does not shave. And the kohĕn shall shut up the eruption another seven days.
13.34: “And on the seventh day the kohĕn shall look at the eruption and see, if the eruption has not spread over the skin, and does not appear deeper than the skin, then the kohĕn shall pronounce him clean. And he shall wash his garments, and he shall be clean.
13.35: “But if the eruption spreads further over the skin after his cleansing,
13.36: then the kohĕn shall look at him and see, if the eruption has spread over the skin, the kohĕn need not seek for yellow hair, he is unclean.
13.37: “But if the eruption appears to have stayed, and there is black hair grown up in it, the eruption has healed. He is clean, and the kohĕn shall pronounce him clean.
13.38: “And when a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin of the body, white bright spots,
13.39: then the kohĕn shall look and see, if the bright spots on the skin of the body are dull white, it is a white spot that grows on the skin, he is clean.
13.40: “And when a man loses the hair of his head, he is bald, he is clean.
13.41: “And if the hair has fallen from his forehead, he is bald on the forehead, he is clean.
13.42: “And when there is on the bald head or bald forehead a reddish-white infection, it is leprosy breaking out on his bald head or his bald forehead.
13.43: “And the kohĕn shall look at it and see, if the swelling of the infection is reddish-white on his bald head or on his bald forehead, as the appearance of leprosy on the skin of the body,
13.44: he is a leprous man, he is unclean. The kohĕn shall pronounce him unclean, without fail, his infection is on his head.
13.45: “As for the leper who has the infection, his garments are torn, and his head is uncovered, and he has to cover his upper lip and cry, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’
13.46: “He is unclean - all the days he has the infection he is unclean. He is unclean, and he dwells alone, his dwelling place is outside the camp.
13.47: “And when a garment has an infection of leprosy in it, in a woolen garment or in a linen garment,
13.48: or in the warp or in the weft of linen or wool, or in leather or in any leather-work,
13.49: and the infection shall be greenish or reddish in the garment or in the leather, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object, it is an infection of leprosy and shall be shown to the kohĕn.
13.50: “And the kohĕn shall look at the infection and shut up the infection seven days.
13.51: “And he shall look at the infection on the seventh day. And when the infection has spread in the garment, or in the warp or in the weft, or in the leather or any leather-work, the infection is an active leprosy, it is unclean.
13.52: “And he shall burn that garment, or the warp or the weft, in wool or in linen, or any leather object in which the infection is, for it is an active leprosy. It is burned with fire.
13.53: “But if the kohĕn looks and sees that the infection has not spread in the garment, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object,
13.54: then the kohĕn shall give command, and they shall wash that in which the infection is. And he shall shut it up another seven days.
13.55: “And the kohĕn shall look at the infection after it has been washed and see, if the infection has not changed its appearance, though the infection has not spread, it is unclean, and burn it in the fire - it is eaten away, in its inside or outside.
13.56: “And if the kohĕn shall look and see that the infection has faded after washing it, then he shall tear it out of the garment, or out of the warp, or out of the weft, or out of the leather.
13.57: “And if it is still seen in the garment, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object, it is a spreading infection. Burn it with fire, that in which the infection is.
13.58: “And if you wash the garment, or the warp or the weft, or any leather object, if the infection has disappeared from it, then it shall be washed a second time, and shall be clean.
13.59: “This is the Torah of the infection of leprosy in a garment of wool or linen, or in the warp or in the weft, or in any leather object, to pronounce it clean or to pronounce it unclean.”

14.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
14.2: “This shall be the Torah of the leper for the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought to the kohĕn,
14.3: and the kohĕn shall go out of the camp, and the kohĕn shall look and see, if the leprosy is healed in the leper,
14.4: then the kohĕn shall command, and he shall take for him who is to be cleansed two live and clean birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.
14.5: “And the kohĕn shall command, and he shall kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water.
14.6: “Let him take the live bird and the cedar wood and the scarlet and the hyssop, and dip them and the live bird in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water.
14.7: “And he shall sprinkle it seven times on him who is to be cleansed from the leprosy, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let the live bird loose in the open field.
14.8: “And he who is to be cleansed shall wash his garments, and shall shave off all his hair and wash himself in water, and shall be clean. Then after that he comes into the camp, but shall stay outside his tent seven days.
14.9: “And on the seventh day it shall be that he shaves all the hair off his head and his beard and his eyebrows, even all his hair he shaves off. And he shall wash his garments and wash his body in water, and shall be clean.
14.10: “And on the eighth day he takes two male lambs, perfect ones, and one ewe lamb a year old, a perfect one, and three-tenth parts of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one log of oil.
14.11: “And the kohĕn who is cleansing shall present the man who is to be cleansed, with these, before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
14.12: “And the kohĕn shall take one male lamb and bring it as a guilt offering, and the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.13: “And he shall slaughter the lamb in the place where he slaughters the sin offering and the burnt offering, in a qodesh place. For the guilt offering, like the sin offering, belongs to the kohĕn. It is most qodesh.
14.14: “And the kohĕn shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering, and the kohĕn shall put it on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
14.15: “And the kohĕn shall take some of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.
14.16: “And the kohĕn shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.17: “And of the rest of the oil in his hand, the kohĕn puts some on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the blood of the guilt offering.
14.18: “And the rest of the oil that is in the kohĕn’s hand he puts on the head of him who is to be cleansed. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.19: “And the kohĕn shall make the sin offering, and make atonement for him who is to be cleansed from his uncleanness. Then afterwards he slaughters the burnt offering.
14.20: “And the kohĕn shall offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.
14.21: “But if he is poor and is unable to afford it, then he shall take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one-tenth part of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil,
14.22: and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, such as he is able to afford, and one shall be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
14.23: “And he shall bring them to the kohĕn on the eighth day for his cleansing, to the door of the Tent of Appointment, before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.24: “And the kohĕn shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and the kohĕn shall wave them as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.25: “And he shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the kohĕn shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
14.26: “Then the kohĕn pours some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.
14.27: “And the kohĕn shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.28: “And the kohĕn shall put some of the oil that is in his hand on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of the right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the place of the blood of the guilt offering.
14.29: “And the rest of the oil that is in the kohĕn’s hand he puts on the head of him who is to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.30: “And he shall prepare one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, such as he is able to afford,
14.31: that which he is able to afford, the one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, with the grain offering. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him who is to be cleansed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.32: “This is the Torah for one who had an infection of leprosy, who is unable to afford for his cleansing.”
14.33: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
14.34: “When you come into the land of Kena’an, which I am giving you as a possession, and I put a plague of leprosy in a house in the land of your possession,
14.35: then shall the one who owns the house come and inform the kohĕn, saying, ‘It seems to me that there is some plague in the house.’
14.36: “And the kohĕn shall command, and they shall empty the house, before the kohĕn goes in to look at the plague, so that all that is in the house is not made unclean. And after that the kohĕn goes in to look at the house.
14.37: “And he shall look at the plague and see, if the plague is on the walls of the house with sunken places, greenish or reddish, which appear to be deep in the wall,
14.38: then the kohĕn shall go out of the house, to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days.
14.39: “And the kohĕn shall come again on the seventh day and look and see, if the plague has spread on the walls of the house,
14.40: then the kohĕn shall command, and they shall remove the stones with the plague in them, and they shall throw them outside the city, into an unclean place,
14.41: while he lets the house be scraped inside, all around, and the dust that they scrape off they shall pour out in an unclean place outside the city.
14.42: “And they shall take other stones and put them in the place of those stones, and take other mortar and plaster the house.
14.43: “And if the plague comes back and breaks out in the house, after he has removed the stones, after he has scraped the house, and after it is plastered,
14.44: then the kohĕn shall come and look and see, if the plague has spread in the house, it is an active leprosy in the house, it is unclean.
14.45: “And he shall break down the house, its stones, and its timber, and all the plaster of the house, and he shall bring them outside the city to an unclean place.
14.46: “And he who goes into the house, all the days while it is shut up, becomes unclean until evening.
14.47: “And he who lies down in the house has to wash his garments, and he who eats in the house has to wash his garments.
14.48: “However, if the kohĕn indeed comes in and looks at it and sees that the plague has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, then the kohĕn shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.
14.49: “And to cleanse the house, he shall take two birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.
14.50: “And he shall kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water,
14.51: and he shall take the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the live bird, and dip them in the blood of the slain bird and in the running water, and shall sprinkle the house seven times.
14.52: “He shall thus cleanse the house with the blood of the bird and the running water and the live bird, and with the cedar wood, and with the hyssop, and with the scarlet,
14.53: and he shall let the live bird loose outside the city in the open field, and shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
14.54: “This is the Torah for any infection of leprosy, and eruption,
14.55: and for leprosy of a garment, and of a house,
14.56: and for a swelling, and for a scab, and for a bright spot,
14.57: to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the Torah of leprosy.”

15.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
15.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When any man has a discharge from his flesh, his discharge is unclean.
15.3: ‘And this is his uncleanness in regard to his discharge; whether his flesh runs with his discharge, or his flesh is stopped up by his discharge, it is his uncleanness.
15.4: ‘Any bed becomes unclean on which he who has the discharge lies, and any object on which he sits becomes unclean.
15.5: ‘And anyone who touches his bed has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.6: ‘And he who sits on any object on which he who has the discharge sat, has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.7: ‘And he who touches the flesh of him who has the discharge has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening.
15.8: ‘And when he who has the discharge spits on him who is clean, then he shall wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.9: ‘Any saddle on which he who has the discharge rides becomes unclean.
15.10: ‘And whoever touches any of that which was under him is unclean until evening. And he who is carrying them up has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.11: ‘And anyone whom he who has the discharge touches without rinsing his hands in water, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.12: ‘And the earthen vessel which he who has the discharge touches has to be broken, and every wooden vessel has to be rinsed in water.
15.13: ‘And when he who has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, then he shall count for himself seven days for his cleansing, and shall wash his garments, and shall bathe his flesh in running water, and be clean.
15.14: ‘And on the eighth day he takes for himself two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and shall come before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to the door of the Tent of Appointment, and shall give them to the kohĕn.
15.15: ‘And the kohĕn shall prepare them, the one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 because of his discharge.
15.16: ‘And when a man has an emission of semen, then he shall wash all his flesh in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.17: ‘And any garment and any leather on which there is semen, shall also be washed with water, and be unclean until evening.
15.18: ‘And when a woman lies with a man, and there is an emission of semen, they both shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.19: ‘And when a woman has a discharge, and the discharge from her flesh is blood, she has to be in her separation for seven days. And whoever touches her is unclean until evening.
15.20: ‘And whatever she lies on during her separation is unclean. And whatever she sits on is unclean.
15.21: ‘And anyone who touches her bed has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.22: ‘And whoever touches any object that she sat on has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.23: ‘And if it is on the bed or on any object on which she sits, when he touches it, he is unclean until evening.
15.24: ‘And if any man lies with her at all, and her monthly flow is on him, he shall be unclean seven days. And any bed he lies on is unclean.
15.25: ‘And when a woman has a discharge of blood for many days, other than at the time of her monthly separation, or when she discharges beyond her usual time of monthly separation, all the days of her unclean discharge shall be as the days of her monthly separation. She is unclean.
15.26: ‘Any bed on which she lies all the days of her discharge is to her as the bed of her monthly separation. And whatever she sits on is unclean, as the uncleanness of her monthly separation.
15.27: ‘And anyone who touches them is unclean, and shall wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
15.28: ‘But if she is cleansed of her discharge, then she shall count for herself seven days, and after that she is clean.
15.29: ‘And on the eighth day she takes for herself two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and shall bring them to the kohĕn, to the door of the Tent of Appointment.
15.30: ‘And the kohĕn shall prepare the one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the kohĕn shall make atonement for her before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for the discharge of her uncleanness.
15.31: ‘Thus you shall separate the children of Yisra’ĕl from their uncleanness, lest they die in their uncleanness when they defile My Mishkan which is in their midst.
15.32: ‘This is the Torah for one who has a discharge, and for him who emits semen and is unclean thereby,
15.33: and for her who is sick in her monthly separation, and for one who has a discharge, either man or woman, and for him who lies with an unclean woman.’ ”

16.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh after the death of the two sons of Aharon, when they drew near before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and died.
16.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Speak to Aharon your brother not to come in at all times to the qodesh place inside the veil, before the lid of atonement which is on the ark, lest he die, because I appear in the cloud above the lid of atonement.
16.3: “With this Aharon should come into the qodesh place: with the blood of a young bull as a sin offering, and of a ram as a burnt offering.
16.4: “He should put on the qodesh linen long shirt, with linen trousers on his flesh, and gird himself with a linen girdle, and be dressed with the linen turban - they are qodesh garments. And he shall bathe his body in water, and shall put them on.
16.5: “And from the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl he takes two male goats as a sin offering, and one ram as a burnt offering.
16.6: “And Aharon shall bring the bull as a sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house.
16.7: “And he shall take the two goats and let them stand before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
16.8: “And Aharon shall cast lots for the two goats, one lot for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the other lot for Azazĕl.
16.9: “And Aharon shall bring the goat on which the lot for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fell, and shall prepare it as a sin offering.
16.10: “But the goat on which the lot for Azazĕl fell is caused to stand alive before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to make atonement upon it, to send it into the wilderness to Azazĕl.
16.11: “And Aharon shall bring the bull of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house, and shall slaughter the bull as the sin offering which is for himself,
16.12: and shall take a fire holder filled with burning coals of fire from the altar before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, with his hands filled with sweet incense beaten fine, and shall bring it inside the veil.
16.13: “And he shall put the incense on the fire before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the cloud of incense shall cover the lid of atonement which is on the Witness, lest he die.
16.14: “And he shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the lid of atonement on the east side, also in front of the lid of atonement he sprinkles some of the blood with his finger seven times.
16.15: “And he shall slaughter the goat of the sin offering, which is for the people, and shall bring its blood inside the veil, and shall do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the lid of atonement and in front of the lid of atonement.
16.16: “And he shall make atonement for the qodesh place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and because of their transgressions in all their sins. And so he does for the Tent of Appointment which is dwelling with them in the midst of their uncleanness.
16.17: “And no man should be in the Tent of Appointment when he goes in to make atonement in the qodesh place, until he comes out. And he shall make atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl.
16.18: “And he shall go out to the altar that is before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and make atonement for it. And he shall take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat, and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
16.19: “And he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and qadosh it from the uncleanness of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
16.20: “And when he has finished atoning for the qodesh place, and the Tent of Appointment, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat.
16.21: “Then Aharon shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat, and shall confess over it all the wickednesses of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and all their transgressions in all their sins, and shall put them on the head of the goat, and shall send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a fit man.
16.22: “And the goat shall bear on itself all their wickednesses, to a land cut off. Thus he shall send the goat away into the wilderness.
16.23: “Aharon shall then come into the Tent of Appointment, and shall take off the linen garments which he put on when he went into the qodesh place, and shall leave them there.
16.24: “And he shall bathe his body in water in the qodesh place, and shall put on his garments, and shall come out and prepare his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people,
16.25: and burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
16.26: “And he who sent away the goat to Azazĕl washes his garments, and shall bathe his body in water, and afterward he comes into the camp.
16.27: “And the bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the qodesh place, is brought outside the camp. And they shall burn their skins, and their flesh, and their dung with fire.
16.28: “And he who burns them washes his garments, and shall bathe his body in water, and afterward he comes into the camp.
16.29: “And this shall be for you a Law forever: In the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you afflict your beings, and do no work, the native or the stranger who sojourns among you.
16.30: “For on that day he makes atonement for you, to cleanse you, to be clean from all your sins before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
16.31: “It is a Shabbath of rest for you, and you shall afflict your beings - a Law forever.
16.32: “And the kohĕn, who is anointed and ordained to serve as kohĕn in his father’s place, shall make atonement, and shall put on the linen garments, the qodesh garments,
16.33: and he shall make atonement for the Qodesh Miqdash, and make atonement for the Tent of Appointment and for the altar, and make atonement for the kohenim and for all the people of the assembly.
16.34: “And this shall be for you a Law forever, to make atonement for the children of Yisra’ĕl, for all their sins, once a year.” And he did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh.

17.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
17.2: “Speak to Aharon, to his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘This is the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded, saying,
17.3: “Any man from the house of Yisra’ĕl who slaughters a bull or a lamb or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,
17.4: and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Appointment, to bring an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 before the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, blood-guilt is reckoned to that man. He has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people,
17.5: in order that the children of Yisra’ĕl bring their slaughterings which they slaughter in the open field. And they shall bring them to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at the door of the Tent of Appointment, to the kohĕn, and slaughter them as peace offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.6: “And the kohĕn shall sprinkle the blood on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at the door of the Tent of Appointment, and shall burn the fat for a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.7: “And let them no longer slaughter their slaughterings to demons, after whom they whored. This is a Law forever for them throughout their generations.” ’
17.8: “And say to them, ‘Any man of the house of Yisra’ĕl, or of the strangers who sojourn among you, who offers a burnt offering or slaughtering,
17.9: and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Appointment, to do it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that man shall be cut off from among his people.
17.10: ‘And any man of the house of Yisra’ĕl, or of the strangers who sojourn among you, who eats any blood, I shall turn My face against that being who eats blood, and shall cut him off from among his people.
17.11: ‘For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives, for it is the blood that makes atonement for the life.’
17.12: “Therefore I said to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘No being among you eats blood, nor does any stranger who sojourns among you eat blood.’
17.13: “And any man from the children of Yisra’ĕl, or from the strangers who sojourn among you, who hunts and catches any beast or bird, which is eaten, shall pour out its blood and cover it with dust,
17.14: for it is the life of all flesh. Its blood is for its life. And I said to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Do not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone eating it is cut off.’
17.15: “And any being who eats a carcass or what was torn by a beast, be he a native or a stranger, he shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening. Then he shall be clean.
17.16: “And if he does not wash or bathe his body, then he shall bear his wickedness.”

18.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
18.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
18.3: ‘Do not do as they do in the land of Mitsrayim, where you dwelt. And do not do as they do in the land of Kena’an, where I am bringing you, and do not walk in their laws.
18.4: ‘Do My Right-Rulings and guard My Laws, to walk in them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
18.5: ‘And you shall guard My Laws and My Right-Rulings, which a man does and lives by them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.6: ‘No one is to approach anyone of his own flesh to uncover his nakedness. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.7: ‘The nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother you do not uncover. She is your mother, you do not uncover her nakedness.
18.8: ‘The nakedness of your father’s wife you do not uncover, it is your father’s nakedness.
18.9: ‘The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father, or the daughter of your mother, whether born at home or elsewhere, their nakedness you do not uncover.
18.10: ‘The nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, their nakedness you do not uncover, for theirs is your own nakedness.
18.11: ‘The nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, brought forth by your father, she is your sister, you do not uncover her nakedness.
18.12: ‘The nakedness of your father’s sister you do not uncover, she is your father’s flesh.
18.13: ‘The nakedness of your mother’s sister you do not uncover, for she is your mother’s flesh.
18.14: ‘The nakedness of your father’s brother you do not uncover, you do not approach his wife, she is your aunt.
18.15: ‘The nakedness of your daughter-in-law you do not uncover, she is your son’s wife, you do not uncover her nakedness.
18.16: ‘The nakedness of your brother’s wife you do not uncover, it is your brother’s nakedness.
18.17: ‘The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you do not uncover, nor do you take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter, to uncover her nakedness. They are her relatives - it is wickedness.
18.18: ‘And do not take a woman as a rival to her sister, to uncover her nakedness while the other is alive.
18.19: ‘And do not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness in her monthly separation of uncleanness.
18.20: ‘And do not have intercourse with the wife of your neighbor, to defile yourself with her.
18.21: ‘And do not give any of your offspring to pass through to Moleḵ. And do not profane the Name of your Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.22: ‘And do not lie with a male as with a woman, it is an abomination.
18.23: ‘And do not have intercourse with any beast, to defile yourself with it. And a woman does not stand before a beast to mate with it, it is a perversion.
18.24: ‘Do not defile yourselves with all these, for by all these the nations are defiled, which I am driving out before you.
18.25: ‘Thus the land became defiled, therefore I punished it for its wickedness, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
18.26: ‘But you, you shall guard My Laws and My Right-Rulings, and not do any of these abominations, the native nor stranger who sojourns among you,
18.27: because the men of the land who were before you have done all these abominations, and thus the land became defiled.
18.28: ‘So let not the land vomit you out for defiling it, as it vomited out the nations that were before you.
18.29: ‘For whoever does any of these abominations, those beings who do them shall be cut off from among their people.
18.30: ‘And you shall guard My Charge, so as not to do any of these abominable practices which were done before you, so as not to defile yourselves by them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.’ ”

19.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
19.2: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘Be qodesh, for I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim am qodesh.
19.3: ‘Each one of you should revere his mother and his father, and guard My Shabbathoth. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
19.4: ‘Do not turn to idols, and do not make for yourselves molded mighty ones. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
19.5: ‘And when you bring a peace offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, bring it for your acceptance.
19.6: ‘It is eaten the same day you slaughter it, and on the next day. And that which is left on the third day is burned with fire.
19.7: ‘So if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is abominable, it is not accepted,
19.8: and he who eats it bears his wickedness, because he has profaned the qodesh offering of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and that being shall be cut off from his people.
19.9: ‘And when you reap the harvest of your land, do not completely reap the corners of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
19.10: ‘And do not glean your vineyard or gather every grape of your vineyard, leave them for the poor and the stranger. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
19.11: ‘Do not steal, do not lie, do not deceive one another.
19.12: ‘And do not swear falsely by My Name and so profane the Name of your Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.13: ‘Do not oppress your neighbor and do not rob the wages of him who is hired. It is not to remain with you all night until morning.
19.14: ‘Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling-block before the blind, but revere your Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.15: ‘Do no unrighteousness in right-ruling. Do not be partial to the poor or favor the face of the great, but rightly rule your neighbor in righteousness.
19.16: ‘Do not go slandering among your people. Do not stand against the blood of your neighbor. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.17: ‘Do not hate your brother in your heart. Reprove your neighbor, for certain, and bear no sin because of him.
19.18: ‘Do not take vengeance or bear a grudge against the children of your people. And you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.19: ‘Guard My Laws. Do not let your livestock mate with another kind. Do not sow your field with mixed seed. And do not put a garment woven of two sorts of thread upon you.
19.20: ‘And when a man has intercourse with a woman who is a female servant, engaged to a man, and who has not at all been ransomed nor redeemed, nor freedom given there should be an inquiry. But they are not put to death, because she was not free.
19.21: ‘And he shall bring his guilt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to the door of the Tent of Appointment, a ram as a guilt offering.
19.22: ‘And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for his sin which he has done. And the sin which he has sinned shall be forgiven him.
19.23: ‘And when you come into the land, and have planted all kinds of trees for food, then you shall reckon their fruit as uncircumcised. For three years it is as uncircumcised to you, it is not eaten.
19.24: ‘And in the fourth year all its fruit is qodesh - praises to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.25: ‘And in the fifth year you eat its fruit, so that it increases its yield to you. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
19.26: ‘Do not eat with the blood. Do not practice divination or magic.
19.27: ‘Do not round the corner of your head, nor destroy the corner of your beard.
19.28: ‘And do not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor put tattoo marks on you. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.29: ‘Do not profane your daughter by making her a whore, so that the land does not whore, and the land becomes filled with wickedness.
19.30: ‘Guard My Shabbathoth and reverence My Miqdash. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.31: ‘Do not turn to mediums, and do not seek after spiritists to be defiled by them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
19.32: ‘Rise up before the grey-headed. And you shall favor the face of an old man, and shall revere your Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.33: ‘And when a stranger sojourns with you in your land, do not oppress him.
19.34: ‘Let the stranger who dwells among you be to you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself. For you were strangers in the land of Mitsrayim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
19.35: ‘Do no unrighteousness in right-ruling, in measurement of length, in weight, or in measuring liquids.
19.36: ‘Have right scales, right weights, a right ĕphah, and a right hin. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim.
19.37: ‘And you shall guard all My Laws and all My Right-Rulings, and do them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”

2.1: ‘And when anyone brings a grain offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, his offering is to be of fine flour. And he shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it,
2.2: and he shall bring it to the sons of Aharon, the kohenim, and he shall take from it his hand filled with fine flour and oil with all the frankincense. And the kohĕn shall burn it as a remembrance portion on the altar, an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.3: ‘And the rest of the grain offering is for Aharon and his sons, most qodesh of the offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by fire.
2.4: ‘And so you bring as an offering a grain offering baked in the oven, unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened thin cakes anointed with oil.
2.5: ‘But if your offering is a grain offering on the griddle, it is of fine flour, unleavened, mixed with oil.
2.6: ‘Divide it into bits and pour oil on it, it is a grain offering.
2.7: ‘And if your offering is a grain offering, in a stewing-pot, it is made of fine flour with oil.
2.8: ‘And you shall bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the grain offering that is made of these, and shall present it to the kohĕn, and he shall bring it to the altar.
2.9: ‘And the kohĕn shall take from the grain offering a remembrance portion, and burn it on the altar, an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.10: ‘And the rest of the grain offering is for Aharon and his sons, most qodesh of the offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made by fire.
2.11: ‘No grain offering which you bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is made with leaven, for you do not burn any leaven or any honey in an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made by fire.
2.12: ‘Bring them to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 as an offering of the first-fruits, but they are not burned on the altar for a sweet fragrance.
2.13: ‘And season with salt every offering of your grain offering, and do not allow the salt of the Covenant of your Elohim to be lacking from your grain offering. With all your offerings you bring salt.
2.14: ‘And if you bring a grain offering of your first-fruits to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, bring for the grain offering of your first-fruits green heads of grain roasted on the fire, crushed heads of new grain.
2.15: ‘And you shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
2.16: ‘And the kohĕn shall burn the remembrance portion, from its crushed grain and from its oil, with all the frankincense, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

20.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
20.2: “Say to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Any man of the children of Yisra’ĕl, or of the strangers who sojourn in Yisra’ĕl, who gives any of his offspring to Moleḵ, shall certainly be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
20.3: ‘And I, I shall turn My face against that man, and shall cut him off from the midst of his people, because he has given of his offspring to Moleḵ, so as to defile My Miqdash and to profane My qodesh Name.
20.4: ‘And if the people of the land at all hide their eyes from the man, as he gives any of his offspring to Moleḵ, and they do not kill him,
20.5: then I shall turn My face against that man and against his clan, and shall cut him off - and all who go whoring after him, even go whoring after Moleḵ - from the midst of their people.
20.6: ‘And the being who turns to mediums, and to spiritists, to go whoring after them, I shall turn My face against that being and cut him off from the midst of his people.
20.7: ‘And you shall qadosh yourselves, and shall be qodesh, for I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
20.8: and you shall guard My Laws and do them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who qadosh you.
20.9: ‘For everyone who curses his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death - he has cursed his father or his mother, his blood is on him.
20.10: ‘And a man who commits adultery with the wife of another man, who commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor: the adulterer and the adulteress shall certainly be put to death.
20.11: ‘And a man who lies with the wife of his father has uncovered the nakedness of his father, both of them shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.
20.12: ‘And a man who lies with his daughter-in-law: both of them shall certainly be put to death, they have made confusion, their blood is upon them.
20.13: ‘And a man who lies with a male as he lies with a woman: both of them have done an abomination, they shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.
20.14: ‘And a man who marries a woman and her mother: it is wickedness, they are burned with fire, both he and they, that there be no wickedness in your midst.
20.15: ‘And a man who has intercourse with a beast: he shall certainly be put to death, and the beast you kill.
20.16: ‘And a woman who approaches any beast and mates with it: you shall kill the woman and the beast, they shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.
20.17: ‘And a man who takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness: it is a reproach, and they shall be cut off before the eyes of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness, he bears his wickedness.
20.18: ‘And a man who lies with a woman during her sickness and uncovers her nakedness: he has laid bare her flow, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood, both of them shall be cut off from the midst of their people.
20.19: ‘And do not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister nor of your father’s sister, for that is laying bare one’s own flesh, they bear their wickedness.
20.20: ‘And a man who lies with his uncle’s wife: he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness, they bear their sin, they die childless.
20.21: ‘And a man who takes his brother’s wife: it is uncleanness, he has uncovered his brother’s nakedness, they are childless.
20.22: ‘And you shall guard all My Laws and all My Right-Rulings, and do them, so that the land where I am bringing you to dwell does not vomit you out.
20.23: ‘And do not walk in the laws of the nation which I am driving out before you, for they do all these, and therefore I loathed them.
20.24: ‘But I say to you, “You are going to possess their land, and I Myself give it to you to possess it, a land flowing with milk and honey.” I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who has separated you from the peoples.
20.25: ‘And you shall make a distinction between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean birds and clean. And do not make yourselves abominable by beast or by bird, or whatever creeps on the ground, which I have separated from you as unclean.
20.26: ‘And you shall be qodesh to Me, for I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 am qodesh, and have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.
20.27: ‘And a man or a woman in whom there is a medium, or who are spiritists, shall certainly be put to death, they are to stone them with stones. Their blood is upon them.’ ”

21.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Speak to the kohenim, the sons of Aharon, and say to them, ‘No one is to be defiled for the dead among his people,
21.2: except for his relatives who are nearest to him: for his mother, and for his father, and for his son, and for his daughter, and for his brother;
21.3: and for his maiden sister who is near to him, who has had no husband - for her he is defiled.
21.4: ‘A leader does not defile himself among his people, to profane himself;
21.5: they do not make any bald place on their heads, and they do not shave the corner of their beard, and they do not make a cutting in their flesh.
21.6: ‘They are qodesh to their Elohim and do not profane the Name of their Elohim, for they bring the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made by fire, and the bread of their Elohim, and shall be qodesh.
21.7: ‘They do not take a woman who is a whore or a defiled woman, and they do not take a woman put away from her husband, for he is qodesh to his Elohim.
21.8: ‘And you shall qadosh him, for he brings the bread of your Elohim, he is qodesh to you. For I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who qadosh you, am qodesh.
21.9: ‘And when the daughter of any kohĕn profanes herself by whoring, she profanes her father. She is burned with fire.
21.10: ‘And the kohĕn ha’gadol among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil was poured and who is ordained to wear the garments, does not unbind his head nor tear his garments,
21.11: nor come near any dead body, nor defile himself for his father or his mother,
21.12: nor go out of the Miqdash, nor profane the Miqdash of his Elohim, for the sign of dedication of the anointing oil of his Elohim is upon him. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.13: ‘And let him take a wife in her maidenhood.
21.14: ‘A widow or one put away or a defiled woman or a whore - these he does not take. But a maiden of his own people he takes as a wife.
21.15: ‘And he does not profane his offspring among his people, for I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who qadosh him.’ ”
21.16: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
21.17: “Speak to Aharon, saying, ‘No man of your offspring throughout their generations, who has any defect, is to draw near to bring the bread of his Elohim.
21.18: ‘For any man who has a defect is not to draw near: a man blind or one lame or disfigured or deformed,
21.19: a man who has a broken foot or broken hand,
21.20: or is a hunchback or a dwarf, or a man who has a defect in his eye, or eczema or scab, or is a eunuch.
21.21: ‘No man among the offspring of Aharon the kohĕn, who has a defect, is to come near to bring the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - he has a defect, he does not come near to bring the bread of his Elohim.
21.22: ‘He eats the bread of his Elohim, both the most qodesh and the qodesh,
21.23: only, he does not go near the veil or approach the altar, because he has a defect, lest he profanes My Miqdashim. For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who qadosh them.’ ”
21.24: Thus Mosheh spoke to Aharon and his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ĕl.

22.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
22.2: “Speak to Aharon and his sons, that they separate themselves from the qodesh offerings of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and that they do not profane My qodesh Name in what they qadosh to Me. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.3: “Say to them, ‘Any man of all your offspring throughout your generations who draws near the qodesh offerings which the children of Yisra’ĕl qadosh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, while he has uncleanness upon him, that being shall be cut off from before Me. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.4: ‘Any man of the offspring of Aharon, who is a leper or has a discharge, does not eat the qodesh offerings until he is clean. And whoever touches what is rendered unclean by a corpse, or a man who has had an emission of semen,
22.5: or a man who touches any creeping creature by which he would be made unclean, or any being by whom he would become unclean, even any of his uncleanness;
22.6: the being who has touched it shall be unclean until evening, and does not eat the qodesh offerings, but shall bathe his body in water.
22.7: ‘And when the sun goes down he shall be clean, and afterward eat the qodesh offerings, because it is his food.
22.8: ‘He does not eat that which dies or is torn by beasts, becoming unclean by it. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.9: ‘And they shall guard My Charge, lest they bear sin for it and die thereby, when they profane it. I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 qadosh them.
22.10: ‘And no stranger eats the qodesh offering. A sojourner with the kohĕn, or a hired servant, does not eat the qodesh offering.
22.11: ‘But when the kohĕn buys a being with his silver, he eats of it. And one who is born in his house eats his food.
22.12: ‘And when a kohĕn’s daughter is married to a stranger, she does not eat of the qodesh offerings.
22.13: ‘But when a kohĕn’s daughter is a widow or put away, and has no child, and has returned to her father’s house as in her youth, she eats her father’s food, but no stranger eats of it.
22.14: ‘And when a man eats the qodesh offering by mistake, then he shall give a qodesh offering to the kohĕn, and add one-fifth to it.
22.15: ‘And do not profane the qodesh offerings of the children of Yisra’ĕl, which they lift up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
22.16: or allow them to bear the wickedness of trespass when they eat their qodesh offerings. For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who qadosh them.’ ”
22.17: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
22.18: “Speak to Aharon and his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘Any man of the house of Yisra’ĕl, or of the strangers in Yisra’ĕl, who brings his offering for any of his vows or for any of his voluntary offerings, which they bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 as a burnt offering,
22.19: for your acceptance, is a male, a perfect one from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.
22.20: ‘Whatever has a defect, you do not bring, for it is not acceptable for you.
22.21: ‘And when a man brings a peace offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to complete a vow, or a voluntary offering from the cattle or the sheep, it is to be perfect to be accepted, let there be no defect in it.
22.22: ‘Those blind or broken or having a cut, or have an ulcer or eczema or scabs, you do not bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, nor make an offering by fire of them on the altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.23: ‘As for a bull or a lamb that has any limb deformed or dwarfed you do prepare as a voluntary offering, but for a vow it is not accepted.
22.24: ‘Do not bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 what is bruised or crushed, or torn or cut, nor do it in your land.
22.25: ‘And from a son of a stranger’s hand you do not bring any of these as the bread of your Elohim, for their corruption is in them, and defects are in them, they are not acceptable for you.’ ”
22.26: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
22.27: “When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall be seven days with its mother. And from the eighth day and thereafter it is acceptable as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.28: “But do not slaughter a cow or a sheep and its young on the same day.
22.29: “And when you bring a slaughtering of thanksgiving to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, bring it for your acceptance.
22.30: “It is eaten that same day, leave none of it till morning. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.31: “And you shall guard My Commands and do them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.32: “And do not profane My qodesh Name, and I shall be qodesh among the children of Yisra’ĕl. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who qadosh you,
22.33: who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be your Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

23.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
23.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘The Appointed Times of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which you are to proclaim as qodesh gatherings, My Appointed Times, are these:
23.3: ‘Six days work is done, but the seventh day is a Shabbath of rest, a qodesh gathering. You do no work, it is a Shabbath to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in all your dwellings.
23.4: ‘These are the Appointed Times of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, qodesh gatherings which you are to proclaim at their Appointed Times.
23.5: ‘In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, is the Pesaḥ to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.6: ‘And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Festival of Matstsoth to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - seven days you eat unleavened bread.
23.7: ‘On the first day you have a qodesh gathering, you do no servile work.
23.8: ‘And you shall bring an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for seven days. On the seventh day is a qodesh gathering, you do no servile work.’ ”
23.9: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
23.10: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and you shall say to them, ‘When you come into the land which I give you, and shall reap its harvest, then you shall bring a sheaf of the first-fruits of your harvest to the kohĕn.
23.11: ‘And he shall wave the sheaf before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for your acceptance. On the morrow after the Shabbath the kohĕn waves it.
23.12: ‘And on that day when you wave the sheaf, you shall prepare a male lamb a year old, a perfect one, as a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
23.13: and its grain offering: two-tenths of an ĕphah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, a sweet fragrance, and its drink offering: one-fourth of a hin of wine.
23.14: ‘And you do not eat bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until the same day that you have brought an offering to your Elohim - a Law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
23.15: ‘And from the morrow after the Shabbath, from the day that you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, you shall count for yourselves: seven completed Shabbathoth.
23.16: ‘Until the morrow after the seventh Shabbath you count fifty days, then you shall bring a new grain offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.17: ‘Bring from your dwellings for a wave offering two of bread, of two-tenth parts of fine flour they are, baked with leaven, first-fruits to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.18: ‘And besides the bread, you shall bring seven lambs a year old, perfect ones, and one young bull and two rams. They are a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering made by fire for a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.19: ‘And you shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two male lambs a year old, as a peace offering.
23.20: ‘And the kohĕn shall wave them, besides the bread of the first-fruits, as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, besides the two lambs. They are qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for the kohĕn.
23.21: ‘And on this same day you shall proclaim a qodesh gathering for yourselves, you do no servile work on it - a Law forever in all your dwellings throughout your generations.
23.22: ‘And when you reap the harvest of your land do not completely reap the corners of your field when you reap, and do not gather any gleaning from your harvest. Leave them for the poor and for the stranger. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.’ ”
23.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
23.24: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you have a rest, a remembrance of blowing of trumpets, a qodesh gathering.
23.25: ‘You do no servile work, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”
23.26: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
23.27: “On the tenth day of this seventh month is Yom ha’Kippurim. It shall be a qodesh gathering for you. And you shall afflict your beings, and shall bring an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.28: “And you do no work on that same day, for it is a Yom Kippurim, to make atonement for you before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
23.29: “For any being who is not afflicted on that same day, he shall be cut off from his people.
23.30: “And any being who does any work on that same day, that being I shall destroy from the midst of his people.
23.31: “You do no work - a Law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
23.32: “It is a Shabbath of rest to you, and you shall afflict your beings. On the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you observe your Shabbath.”
23.33: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
23.34: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Sukkoth for seven days to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.35: ‘On the first day is a qodesh gathering, you do no servile work.
23.36: ‘For seven days you bring an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. On the eighth day there shall be a qodesh gathering for you, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It is a closing Festival, you do no servile work.
23.37: ‘These are the Appointed Times of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which you proclaim as qodesh gatherings, to bring an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, a burnt offering and a grain offering, a slaughtering and drink offerings, as commanded for every day -
23.38: besides the Shabbathoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your voluntary offerings which you give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.39: ‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather in the fruit of the land, celebrate the Festival of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for seven days. On the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day a rest.
23.40: ‘And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of good trees, branches of palm trees, twigs of leafy trees, and willows of the stream, and shall rejoice before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim for seven days.
23.41: ‘And you shall celebrate it as a Festival to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for seven days in the year - a Law forever in your generations. Celebrate it in the seventh month.
23.42: ‘Dwell in booths for seven days; all who are native Yisra’ĕlites dwell in booths,
23.43: so that your generations know that I made the children of Yisra’ĕl dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.’ ”
23.44: Thus did Mosheh speak of the Appointed Times of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to the children of Yisra’ĕl.

24.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
24.2: “Command the children of Yisra’ĕl that they bring to you clear oil of pressed olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.
24.3: “Outside the veil of the Witness, in the Tent of Appointment, Aharon is to arrange it from evening until morning before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 continually - a Law forever throughout your generations.
24.4: “He is to arrange the lamps on the clean gold lampstand before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 continually.
24.5: “And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with it, two-tenth parts in each cake.
24.6: “And you shall put them in two rows, six in a row, on the clean table before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.7: “And you shall put clear frankincense on each row, and it shall be on the bread as a remembrance portion, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.8: “On every Shabbath he is to arrange it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 continually, from the children of Yisra’ĕl - an everlasting Covenant.
24.9: “And it shall be for Aharon and his sons, and they shall eat it in the qodesh place, because it is most qodesh to him from the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made by fire - an everlasting Law.”
24.10: And the son of an Yisra’ĕlite woman, whose father was a Mitsrite, went out among the children of Yisra’ĕl. And the Yisra’ĕlite woman’s son and a man of Yisra’ĕl strove in the camp.
24.11: And the Yisra’ĕlite woman’s son blasphemed the Name, and cursed. So they brought him to Mosheh. Now his mother’s name was Shelomith the daughter of Diḇri, of the tribe of Dan.
24.12: And they put him in under guard, that it might be declared to them at the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.13: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
24.14: “Bring the one who has cursed outside the camp, and all those who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and all the congregation shall stone him.
24.15: “And speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Anyone who curses his Elohim shall bear his sin.
24.16: ‘And he who blasphemes the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall certainly be put to death, and all the congregation certainly stone him, the stranger as well as the native. When he blasphemes the Name, he is put to death.
24.17: ‘And he who smites the life from any man shall certainly be put to death.
24.18: ‘And he who smites a beast repays it, body for body.
24.19: ‘And when a man inflicts a blemish upon his neighbor, as he has done so it is done to him:
24.20: ‘Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he inflicts a blemish upon him, so it is done to him.
24.21: ‘And he who smites a beast repays it, and he who kills a man is put to death.
24.22: ‘You are to have one Right-Ruling, for the stranger and for the native, for I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.’ ”
24.23: And Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and they brought the one who cursed outside the camp, and stoned him with stones. And the children of Yisra’ĕl did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh.

25.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh on Mount Sinai, saying,
25.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land which I give you, then the land shall observe a Shabbath to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
25.3: ‘Six years you sow your field, and six years you prune your vineyard, and gather in its fruit,
25.4: but in the seventh year the land is to have a Shabbath of rest, a Shabbath to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Do not sow your field and do not prune your vineyard.
25.5: ‘Do not reap what grows of its own of your harvest, and do not gather the grapes of your unpruned vine, for it is a year of rest for the land.
25.6: ‘And the Shabbath of the land shall be to you for food, for you and your servant, and for your female servant and your hired servant, and for the stranger who sojourns with you,
25.7: and for your livestock and the beasts that are in your land. All its crops are for food.
25.8: ‘And you shall count seven Shabbathoth of years for yourself, seven times seven years. And the time of the seven Shabbathoth of years shall be to you forty-nine years.
25.9: ‘You shall then sound a ram’s horn to pass through on the tenth day of the seventh month, on Yom ha’Kippurim cause a ram’s horn to pass through all your land.
25.10: ‘And you shall qadosh the fiftieth year, and proclaim release throughout all the land to all its inhabitants, it is a Yoḇĕl for you. And each of you shall return to his possession, and each of you return to his clan.
25.11: ‘The fiftieth year is a Yoḇĕl to you. Do not sow, nor reap what grows of its own, nor gather from its unpruned vine.
25.12: ‘It is a Yoḇĕl, it is qodesh to you. Eat from the field its crops.
25.13: ‘In the Year of this Yoḇĕl let each one of you return to his possession.
25.14: ‘And when you sell whatever to your neighbor or buy from the hand of your neighbor, do not exploit one another.
25.15: ‘According to the number of years after the Yoḇĕl you buy from your neighbor, and according to the number of years of crops he sells to you.
25.16: ‘According to the greater number of years you increase its price, and according to the fewer number of years you diminish its price, because he sells to you according to the number of the years of the crops.
25.17: ‘And do not oppress one another, but you shall revere your Elohim. For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
25.18: ‘And you shall do My Laws and guard My Right-Rulings, and shall do them. And you shall dwell in the land in safety,
25.19: and the land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat to satisfaction, and shall dwell there in safety.
25.20: ‘And since you might say, “What do we eat in the seventh year, since we do not sow nor gather in our crops?”
25.21: ‘Therefore I have commanded My beraḵah on you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth the crop for three years.
25.22: ‘And you shall sow in the eighth year, and eat of the old crop until the ninth year. Eat of the old until its crop comes in.
25.23: ‘And the land is not to be sold beyond reclaim, for the land is Mine, for you are sojourners and settlers with Me.
25.24: ‘And provide for a redemption for the land, in all the land of your possession.
25.25: ‘When your brother becomes poor, and has sold some of his possession, and his redeemer, a close relative comes to redeem it, then he shall redeem what his brother sold.
25.26: ‘And when the man has no one to redeem it, but he himself becomes able to redeem it,
25.27: then let him count the years since its sale, and return the remainder to the man to whom he sold it, that he shall return to his possession.
25.28: ‘And if his hand has not found enough to give back to him, then what was sold shall remain in the hand of him who bought it until the Year of Yoḇĕl. And it shall be released in the Yoḇĕl, and he shall return to his possession.
25.29: ‘And when a man sells a house in a walled city, then his right of redemption shall be at the end of the year after it is sold. His right of redemption lasts a year.
