25.30: ‘But if it is not redeemed within a complete year, then the house in the walled city shall be established beyond reclaim to the buyer of it, throughout his generations. It is not released in the Yoḇĕl.
25.31: ‘The houses of villages, however, which have no wall around them are reckoned as the field of the country. A right of redemption belongs to it, and they are released in the Yoḇĕl.
25.32: ‘As for the cities of the Lĕwites, and the houses in the cities of their possession, the Lĕwites have a right of redemption forever.
25.33: ‘And that which is redeemed from the Lĕwites, both the sale of a house and the city of his possession shall be released in the Year of Yoḇĕl, because the houses in the cities of the Lĕwites are their possession in the midst of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
25.34: ‘But the field of the open land of their cities is not sold, for it is their everlasting possession.
25.35: ‘And when your brother becomes poor, and his hand has failed with you, then you shall sustain him, and he shall live with you, like a stranger or a sojourner.
25.36: ‘Take no interest from him, or profit, but you shall revere your Elohim, and your brother shall live with you.
25.37: ‘Do not lend him your silver on interest, and do not lend him your food for profit.
25.38: ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to give you the land of Kena’an, to be your Elohim.
25.39: ‘And when your brother who dwells by you becomes poor, and sells himself to you, do not make him serve as a slave.
25.40: ‘But as a hired servant, as a settler he is with you, and serves you until the Year of Yoḇĕl.
25.41: ‘And then he shall leave you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own clan, even return to the possession of his fathers.
25.42: ‘For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Mitsrayim, they are not sold as slaves.
25.43: ‘Do not rule over him with harshness, but you shall revere your Elohim.
25.44: ‘And your male and female slaves whom you have from the nations that are around you, from them you buy male and female slaves,
25.45: and also from the sons of the strangers sojourning among you, from them you buy, and from their clans who are with you, which they shall bring forth in your land, and they shall be your property.
25.46: ‘And you shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them as a possession, they are your slaves for all time. But over your brothers, the children of Yisra’ĕl, you do not rule with harshness, one over another.
25.47: ‘Now when a sojourner or a settler with you becomes rich, and your brother with him becomes poor, and sells himself to the settler or sojourner with you, or to a member of the sojourner’s clan,
25.48: after he has been sold, there is a right of redemption to him - one of his brothers redeems him,
25.49: or his uncle or his uncle’s son redeems him, or anyone who is a close relative to him in his clan redeems him, or if he is able, then he shall redeem himself.
25.50: ‘And he shall reckon with him who bought him: The price of his release shall be according to the number of years, from the year that he was sold to him until the Year of Yoḇĕl; as the days of a hired servant it is with him.
25.51: ‘If there are yet many years, according to them he repays the price of his redemption, from the silver of his purchase.
25.52: ‘And if few years are left until the Year of Yoḇĕl, then he shall reckon with him, and according to his years he repays him the price of his redemption.
25.53: ‘He is with him as a yearly hired servant, and he does not rule with harshness over him before your eyes.
25.54: ‘And if he is not redeemed in these years, then he shall be released in the Year of Yoḇĕl, he and his children with him.
25.55: ‘Because the children of Yisra’ĕl are servants to Me, they are My servants whom I brought out of the land of Mitsrayim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.

26.1: ‘Do not make idols for yourselves, and do not put up a carved image or a pillar for yourselves, and do not place a stone image in your land, to bow down to it. For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.
26.2: ‘Guard My Shabbathoth and reverence My Miqdash. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.3: ‘If you walk in My Laws and guard My Commands, and shall do them,
26.4: then I shall give you rain in its season, and the land shall yield its crops, and the trees of the field yield their fruit.
26.5: ‘And your threshing shall last till the time of the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall last till the time of sowing. And you shall eat your bread until you have enough, and shall dwell in your land safely.
26.6: ‘And I shall give peace in the land, and you shall lie down and no one make you afraid. And I shall clear the land of evil beasts, and not let the sword go through your land.
26.7: ‘And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall by the sword before you.
26.8: ‘And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you pursue ten thousand. And your enemies shall fall by the sword before you.
26.9: ‘And I shall turn to you and make you bear fruit, and shall increase you, and shall establish My Covenant with you.
26.10: ‘And you shall eat the old supply, and clear out the old because of the new.
26.11: ‘And I shall put My Mishkan in your midst, and My being shall not reject you.
26.12: ‘And I shall walk in your midst, and shall be your Elohim, and you shall be My people.
26.13: ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from being their slaves. And I have broken the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
26.14: ‘But if you do not obey Me, and do not do all these Commands,
26.15: and if you reject My Laws, or if your being loathes My Right-Rulings, so that you do not do all My Commands, but break My Covenant,
26.16: ‘I also do this to you: And I shall appoint sudden alarm over you, wasting disease and inflammation, destroying the eyes, and consuming the life. And you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.
26.17: ‘And I shall turn My face against you, and you shall be smitten before your enemies. And those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
26.18: ‘And after all these, if you do not obey Me, then I shall punish you seven times more for your sins.
26.19: ‘And I shall break the pride of your power, and shall make your shamayim like iron and your earth like bronze.
26.20: ‘And your strength shall be spent in vain and your land not yield its crops, nor the trees of the land yield their fruit.
26.21: ‘And if you walk contrary to Me, and refuse to obey Me, I shall bring on you seven times more plagues, according to your sins,
26.22: and send wild beasts among you, which shall bereave you of your children. And I shall cut off your livestock, and make you few in number, and your highways shall be deserted.
26.23: ‘And if you are not instructed by Me by these, but walk contrary to Me,
26.24: then I also shall walk contrary to you, and I Myself shall smite you seven times for your sins.
26.25: ‘And I shall bring against you a sword executing the vengeance of My Covenant, and you shall gather together in your cities, and I shall send pestilence among you, and you shall be given into the hand of the enemy.
26.26: ‘When I have cut off your supply of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall bring back to you your bread by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied.
26.27: ‘And if in spite of this, you do not obey Me, but walk contrary to Me,
26.28: then I shall walk contrary to you in wrath. And I Myself shall punish you seven times for your sins.
26.29: ‘And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and eat the flesh of your daughters.
26.30: ‘And I shall destroy your high places, and cut down your sun-pillars, and put your carcasses on the carcasses of your idols. And My being shall loathe you.
26.31: ‘And I shall turn your cities into ruins and lay your miqdashim waste, and not smell your sweet fragrances.
26.32: ‘And I shall lay the land waste, and your enemies who dwell in it shall be astonished at it.
26.33: ‘And I shall scatter you among the gentiles and draw out a sword after you. And your land shall be desert and your cities ruins,
26.34: and the land enjoy its Shabbathoth as long as it lies waste and you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land would rest and enjoy its Shabbathoth.
26.35: ‘As long as it lies waste it rests, for the time it did not rest on your Shabbathoth when you dwelt in it.
26.36: ‘And as for those of you who are left, I shall send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, and the sound of a shaken leaf shall cause them to flee. And they shall flee as though retreating from a sword, and they shall fall when no one pursues.
26.37: ‘And they shall stumble over one another, as from before a sword, when no one pursues. And you shall be unable to stand before your enemies.
26.38: ‘And you shall perish among the gentiles, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up,
26.39: and those of you who are left rot away in their wickedness in your enemies’ lands, and also in their fathers’ wickednesses rot away with them.
26.40: ‘But if they confess their wickedness and the wickedness of their fathers, with their trespass in which they trespassed against Me, and that they also have walked contrary to Me,
26.41: and that I also have walked contrary to them and have brought them into the land of their enemies - if their uncircumcised heart is then humbled, and they accept the punishment of their wickedness,
26.42: then I shall remember My Covenant with Ya’aqoḇ, and also My Covenant with Yitsḥaq, and also remember My Covenant with Aḇraham, and remember the land.
26.43: ‘For the land was abandoned by them, and enjoying its Shabbathoth while lying waste without them, and they were paying for their wickedness, because they rejected My Right-Rulings and because their being loathed My Laws.
26.44: ‘And yet for all this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I shall not reject them, nor shall I loathe them so as to destroy them and break My Covenant with them. For I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim.
26.45: ‘Then I shall remember for their sake the Covenant of the ancestors whom I brought out of the land of Mitsrayim before the eyes of the nations to be their Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”
26.46: These are the Laws and the Right-Rulings and the Torot which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made between Himself and the children of Yisra’ĕl on Mount Sinai by the hand of Mosheh.

27.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
27.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When a man separates a vow, by your evaluation of lives unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
27.3: when your evaluation is of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old, then your evaluation shall be fifty sheqels of silver, according to the sheqel of the qodesh place.
27.4: ‘And if it is a female, then your evaluation shall be thirty sheqels;
27.5: and if from five years old up to twenty years old, then your evaluation for a male shall be twenty sheqels, and for a female ten sheqels;
27.6: and if from a month old up to five years old, then your evaluation for a male shall be five sheqels of silver, and for a female your evaluation shall be three sheqels of silver;
27.7: and if from sixty years old and above, if it is a male, then your evaluation shall be fifteen sheqels, and for a female ten sheqels.
27.8: ‘But if he is too poor to pay your evaluation, then he shall present himself before the kohĕn, and the kohĕn shall lay a value for him. According to the ability of him who vowed, the kohĕn shall value him.
27.9: ‘And if it is a beast of which they bring an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all such given to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is qodesh.
27.10: ‘He is not to replace it or exchange it, good for spoilt or spoilt for good. And if he at all exchanges beast for beast, then both it and the one exchanged for it is qodesh.
27.11: ‘And if it is any unclean beast of which they do not bring an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then he shall present the beast before the kohĕn;
27.12: and the kohĕn shall value it, whether it is good or spoilt. According to your evaluation, of the kohĕn, so it shall be.
27.13: ‘But if he indeed redeems it, then he shall add one-fifth to your evaluation.
27.14: ‘And when a man qadosh his house, to be qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then the kohĕn shall value it, whether it is good or spoilt. As the kohĕn values it, so it stands.
27.15: ‘And if he who qadosh it redeems his house, then he shall add one-fifth of the silver of your evaluation to it, and it shall be his.
27.16: ‘And if a man qadosh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 a field he owns, then your evaluation shall be according to the seed for it - a ḥomer of barley seed at fifty sheqels of silver.
27.17: ‘If he qadosh his field from the Year of Yoḇĕl, according to your evaluation it stands.
27.18: ‘But if he qadosh his field after the Yoḇĕl, then the kohĕn shall reckon to him the silver due according to the years that remain till the Year of Yoḇĕl, and it shall be deducted from your evaluation.
27.19: ‘And if he who qadosh the field would redeem it, then he shall add one-fifth of the silver of your evaluation to it, and it shall be his.
27.20: ‘And if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it is no longer redeemed,
27.21: but the field, when it is released in the Yoḇĕl, is qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 as a dedicated field, to be the possession of the kohĕn.
27.22: ‘And if a man qadosh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 a field which he has bought, which is not the field of his possession,
27.23: then the kohĕn shall reckon to him the amount of your evaluation, up to the Year of Yoḇĕl, and he shall give your evaluation on that day, qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
27.24: ‘In the Year of Yoḇĕl the field returns to him from whom he bought it, to him whose is the possession of the land.
27.25: ‘And all your evaluations are to be according to the sheqel of the qodesh place: twenty gĕrahs to the sheqel.
27.26: ‘However, a first-born of the beasts, which is first-born to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, no man qadosh it - whether bull or sheep, it belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
27.27: ‘And if among the unclean beasts, then he shall ransom it according to your evaluation, and shall add one-fifth to it. And if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your evaluation.
27.28: ‘However, whatever a man lays under ban for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of all that he has, man and beast, or the field of his possession, is not sold or redeemed. Whatever is laid under ban is most qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
27.29: ‘No one under the ban, under the ban among men, is ransomed, but shall certainly be put to death.
27.30: ‘And all the tithe of the land - of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the tree - belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It is qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
27.31: ‘If a man indeed redeems any of his tithes, he adds one-fifth to it.
27.32: ‘And the entire tithe of the herd and of the flock, all that passes under the rod, the tenth one is qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
27.33: ‘He does not inquire whether it is good or spoilt, nor doeshe exchange it. And if he exchanges it at all, then both it and the one exchanged for it are qodesh, it is not redeemed.’ ”
27.34: These are the Commands which𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh for the children of Yisra’ĕl on Mount Sinai.

3.1: ‘And if that which he presents is a peace offering, if he is bringing it of the herd, whether male or female, he brings a perfect one before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.2: ‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and slaughter it at the door of the Tent of Appointment. And the sons of Aharon, the kohenim, shall sprinkle the blood on the altar all around.
3.3: ‘And from the peace offering he shall bring an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
3.4: and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them by the loins, and the appendage on the liver which he removes with the kidneys.
3.5: ‘And the sons of Aharon shall burn it on the altar upon the burnt offering, which is on the wood, which is on the fire, as an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.6: ‘And if that which he presents is from the flock, for a peace offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, male or female, he brings a perfect one.
3.7: ‘If he is bringing a lamb as his offering, then he shall bring it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
3.8: and shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Appointment, and the sons of Aharon shall sprinkle its blood on the altar round about.
3.9: ‘And from the peace offering he shall bring near - as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - its fat, all the fat tail which he removes close to the backbone, and the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
3.10: and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the loins, and the appendage on the liver, which he removes with the kidneys.
3.11: ‘And the kohĕn shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.12: ‘And if his offering is a goat, then he shall bring it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
3.13: and shall lay his hand on its head and slaughter it before the Tent of Appointment. And the sons of Aharon shall sprinkle its blood on the altar all around.
3.14: ‘And from it he shall bring his offering, as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
3.15: and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the loins, and the appendage on the liver, which he removes with the kidneys.
3.16: ‘And the kohĕn shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire for a sweet fragrance. All the fat belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.17: ‘An everlasting Law throughout your generations in all your dwellings: you do not eat any fat or any blood.’ ”

4.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
4.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘When a being sins by mistake against any of the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which are not to be done, and shall do any of them:
4.3: ‘If the anointed kohĕn sins, bringing guilt on the people, then he shall bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for his sin which he has sinned a young bull, a perfect one, as a sin offering,
4.4: and he shall bring the bull to the door of the Tent of Appointment before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and shall lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter the bull before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
4.5: ‘And the anointed kohĕn shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it to the Tent of Appointment,
4.6: and the kohĕn shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in front of the veil of the qodesh place.
4.7: ‘And the kohĕn shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet incense before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which is in the Tent of Appointment, and pour all the blood of the bull at the base of the altar of the burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
4.8: ‘Then he takes all the fat of the bull as the sin offering, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat which is on the entrails,
4.9: and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the loins, and the appendage on the liver, which he removes with the kidneys,
4.10: as it was taken from the bull of the peace offering. And the kohĕn shall burn them on the altar of the burnt offering.
4.11: ‘But the skin of the bull, and all its flesh, with its head and legs, its entrails and dung -
4.12: all of the bull - he shall bring outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. Where the ashes are poured out it is burned.
4.13: ‘And if the entire congregation of Yisra’ĕl strays by mistake, and the matter has been hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done any of the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which are not to be done, and shall be guilty,
4.14: when the sin which they have sinned becomes known, then the assembly shall bring a young bull for the sin, and bring it before the Tent of Appointment.
4.15: ‘And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the bull shall be slaughtered before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
4.16: ‘And the anointed kohĕn shall bring some of the bull’s blood to the Tent of Appointment,
4.17: and the kohĕn shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in front of the veil,
4.18: and put some of the blood on the horns of the altar which is before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which is in the Tent of Appointment, and pour all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
4.19: ‘Then he takes all the fat from it and shall burn it on the altar.
4.20: ‘And he shall do with the bull as he did with the bull as a sin offering - so shall he do it. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.
4.21: ‘And he shall bring the bull outside the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is a sin offering for the assembly.
4.22: ‘When a ruler sins, and by mistake has done any of the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim which are not to be done, and shall be guilty,
4.23: or if his sin which he has sinned is made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering a buck of the goats, a male, a perfect one.
4.24: ‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and slaughter it at the place where they slaughter the burnt offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It is a sin offering.
4.25: ‘And the kohĕn shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering,
4.26: and burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the slaughtering of the peace offering. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
4.27: ‘And if any being of the people of the land sins by mistake by doing any of the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which are not to be done, and shall be guilty,
4.28: or if his sin which he has sinned shall be made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering a female goat, a perfect one, for his sin which he has sinned.
4.29: ‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slaughter the sin offering at the place of the burnt offering.
4.30: ‘And the kohĕn shall take some of its blood with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the blood at the base of the altar,
4.31: then remove all its fat, as fat is removed from the slaughtering of the peace offering. And the kohĕn shall burn it on the altar for a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
4.32: ‘And if he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he brings a female, a perfect one.
4.33: ‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where they slaughter the burnt offering.
4.34: ‘And the kohĕn shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the blood at the base of the altar.
4.35: ‘Then he removes all its fat, as the fat of the lamb is removed from the slaughtering of the peace offering. And the kohĕn shall burn it on the altar, according to the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. So the kohĕn shall make atonement for his sin that he has sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.

5.1: ‘And when a being sins in that he has heard the voice of swearing, and is a witness, or has seen, or has known, but does not reveal it, he shall bear his wickedness.
5.2: ‘Or when a being touches any unclean matter, or the carcass of an unclean beast, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of unclean creeping creatures, and it has been hidden from him, he is unclean and guilty.
5.3: ‘Or when he touches uncleanness of man, any of his uncleanness by which he is unclean, and it has been hidden from him, when he shall know it, then he shall be guilty.
5.4: ‘Or when a being swears, speaking rashly with his lips to do evil or to do good, whatever it is that a man swears rashly with an oath, and it has been hidden from him, when he shall know it, then he shall be guilty of one of these.
5.5: ‘And it shall be, when he is guilty of one of these, that he shall confess that in which he has sinned,
5.6: and shall bring his guilt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for his sin which he has sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a female goat as a sin offering. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him, for his sin.
5.7: ‘And if he is unable to bring a lamb, then he shall bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, he who has sinned, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
5.8: ‘And he shall bring them to the kohĕn, who shall bring near that which is for the sin offering first, and wring off its head from its neck, but not sever it.
5.9: ‘And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
5.10: ‘And he shall prepare the second as a burnt offering according to the Right-Ruling, and the kohĕn shall make atonement for him, for his sin which he has sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.
5.11: ‘But if he is unable to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he who sinned shall bring for his offering one-tenth of an ĕphah of fine flour as a sin offering. He puts no oil on it, nor does he put any frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
5.12: ‘And he shall bring it to the kohĕn, and the kohĕn shall take his hand filled with it as a remembrance portion, and burn it on the altar according to the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It is a sin offering.
5.13: ‘And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him, for his sin that he has sinned in any of these, and it shall be forgiven him. And it shall be the kohĕn’s, like a grain offering.’ ”
5.14: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
5.15: “When a being commits a trespass, and has sinned by mistake against the qodesh matters of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then he shall bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 as his guilt offering a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation in sheqels of silver according to the sheqel of the qodesh place, as a guilt offering.
5.16: “And he shall make good for the sin that he has done against that which is qodesh, and shall add one-fifth to it and give it to the kohĕn. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and it shall be forgiven him.
5.17: “And when any being sins, and has done what is not to be done, any of the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, though he knew it not, yet he shall be guilty and shall bear his wickedness.
5.18: “Then he shall bring to the kohĕn a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation, as a guilt offering. And the kohĕn shall make atonement for his mistake he committed unintentionally, though he did not know it, and it shall be forgiven him -
5.19: it is a guilt offering, he was truly guilty before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

6.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
6.2: “When any being sins, and committed a trespass against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and has lied to his neighbor about a deposit, or about a pledge, or about a robbery, or shall extort from his neighbor,
6.3: or has found what was lost and has lied concerning it, or sworn falsely, so that he sins in regard to any one of all these that a man does,
6.4: then it shall be, when he sins, and shall be guilty, that he shall return what he took by robbery, or what he has extorted, or the deposit which was deposited with him, or the lost item which he found,
6.5: or all that about which he swore falsely. He shall repay its total value, add one-fifth more to it, and give it to whom it belongs, on the day of his guilt offering.
6.6: “Then he brings his guilt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation, as a guilt offering, to the kohĕn.
6.7: “And the kohĕn shall make atonement for him before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and he shall be forgiven for whatever he did that made him guilty.”
6.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
6.9: “Command Aharon and his sons, saying, ‘This is the Torah of the burnt offering: This is the burnt offering, because it is burned on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar is kept burning on it.
6.10: ‘And the kohĕn shall put on his linen garment, and put his linen trousers on his body, and shall take up the ashes of the burnt offering which the fire has consumed on the altar, and shall put them beside the altar.
6.11: ‘And he shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and shall bring the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
6.12: ‘And the fire on the altar is kept burning on it, it is not put out. And the kohĕn shall burn wood on it every morning, and arrange the burnt offering on it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings -
6.13: fire is continually kept burning on the altar, it is not put out.
6.14: ‘And this is the Torah of the grain offering: The sons of Aharon shall bring it near before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in front of the altar,
6.15: and shall take from it with his hand from the fine flour of the grain offering, and from its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the grain offering, and shall burn it on the altar for a sweet fragrance, as its remembrance portion to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.16: ‘Then Aharon and his sons eat the rest of it. It is eaten with unleavened bread, in the qodesh place. They eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Appointment.
6.17: ‘It is not baked with leaven. I have given it to them as their portion of My offerings made by fire, it is most qodesh, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
6.18: ‘All the males among the children of Aharon eat it - a Law forever in your generations concerning the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. All that touches them is to be qodesh.’ ”
6.19: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
6.20: “This is the offering of Aharon and his sons, which they bring near to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, beginning on the day when he is anointed: one-tenth of an ĕphah of fine flour as a daily grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it at night.
6.21: “It is made on a griddle with oil. Bring it in mixed, bring the baked portions of the grain offering near, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.22: “And the anointed kohĕn from among his sons, who is in his place, prepares it - a Law forever to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. All of it has to be burned,
6.23: and every grain offering for the kohĕn is completely burned, it is not eaten.”
6.24: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
6.25: “Speak to Aharon and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the Torah of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering is slaughtered before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, it is most qodesh.
6.26: ‘The kohĕn who is making atonement eats it, in the qodesh place it is eaten, in the courtyard of the Tent of Appointment.
6.27: ‘All that touches its flesh is to be qodesh. And when its blood is sprinkled on any garment, you wash that on which it was sprinkled, in a qodesh place.
6.28: ‘But the earthen vessel in which it is cooked is to be broken. And if it is cooked in a bronze pot, then it is scoured and rinsed in water.
6.29: ‘Every male among the kohenim eats it, it is most qodesh.
6.30: ‘And no sin offering from which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Appointment, to make atonement in the qodesh place, is eaten, it is burned with fire.

7.1: ‘And this is the Torah of the guilt offering - it is most qodesh.
7.2: ‘The guilt offering is slaughtered in the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, and its blood is sprinkled on the altar all around.
7.3: ‘Then he brings from it all its fat: the fat tail and the fat that covers the entrails,
7.4: and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the loins, and the appendage on the liver, which he removes with the kidneys.
7.5: ‘And the kohĕn shall burn them on the altar as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It is a guilt offering.
7.6: ‘Every male among the kohenim eats it. It is eaten in the qodesh place, it is most qodesh.
7.7: ‘The guilt offering is like the sin offering, there is one Torah for them both: the kohĕn who makes atonement with it, it is his.
7.8: ‘And the kohĕn who brings anyone’s burnt offering, the skin of the burnt offering which he has brought is the kohĕn’s, it is his.
7.9: ‘And every grain offering that is baked in the oven and all that is prepared in the stewing-pot, or on a griddle, is the kohĕn’s who brings it, it is his.
7.10: ‘And every grain offering mixed with oil, or dry, is for all the sons of Aharon, for all alike.
7.11: ‘And this is the Torah of the slaughtering of peace offerings which is brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄:
7.12: ‘If he brings it for a thanksgiving, then he shall bring with the slaughtering of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened thin cakes anointed with oil, or cakes of finely blended flour mixed with oil.
7.13: ‘Besides the cakes, he brings as his offering leavened bread together with the slaughtering of thanksgiving of his peace offering.
7.14: ‘And from it he shall bring one cake from each offering as a contribution to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: to the kohĕn who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering, it is his.
7.15: ‘As for the flesh of the slaughtering of his peace offering for thanksgiving, it is eaten the same day it is offered, he does not leave any of it until morning.
7.16: ‘And if the offering he brings is a vow or a voluntary offering, it is eaten the same day that he brings his slaughtering, and what is left of it is eaten the next day,
7.17: but whatever is left of the flesh of the slaughtering on the third day is burned with fire.
7.18: ‘However, if any of the flesh of his peace offering is eaten at all on the third day, it is not accepted. It is not reckoned to him who brings it, it is unclean to him, and the being who eats of it bears his wickedness.
7.19: ‘And the flesh that touches that which is unclean is not eaten, it is burned with fire. And as for the clean flesh, all who are clean eat of it.
7.20: ‘But the being who eats the flesh of the peace offering that belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, while he is unclean, that being shall be cut off from his people.
7.21: ‘And when a being who touches that which is unclean, of the uncleanness of man, or of the uncleanness of beast, or of any unclean swarming creature, and shall eat the flesh of the peace offering that belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that being shall be cut off from his people.’ ”
7.22: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
7.23: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Do not eat any fat, of bull or sheep or goat.
7.24: ‘And the fat of a dead body, and the fat of what is torn, is used for any purpose, but you do not eat it at all.
7.25: ‘For whoever eats the fat of the beast of which men bring as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even the being who eats it shall be cut off from his people.
7.26: ‘And do not eat any blood in any of your dwellings, of bird or of beast.
7.27: ‘Any being who eats any blood, even that being shall be cut off from his people.’ ”
7.28: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
7.29: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘He who brings his peace offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brings his offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from the slaughtering of his peace offering.
7.30: ‘With his own hands he brings the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He brings the fat with the breast, to be waved as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.31: ‘And the kohĕn shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast shall be Aharon’s and his sons.’
7.32: ‘And the right thigh you give to the kohĕn as a contribution from your peace offerings.
7.33: ‘He among the sons of Aharon, who brings the blood of the peace offering, and the fat, the right thigh is his for a portion.
7.34: ‘For the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution I have taken from the children of Yisra’ĕl, from their peace offerings, and I give them to Aharon the kohĕn and to his sons, as a Law forever, from the children of Yisra’ĕl.’ ”
7.35: This is the anointed portion for Aharon and the anointed portion for his sons, from the offerings made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, on the day when Mosheh presented them to serve as kohenim to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
7.36: which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded to be given to them by the children of Yisra’ĕl, on the day that He anointed them, a Law forever throughout their generations.
7.37: This is the Torah of the burnt offering, of the grain offering, and of the sin offering, and of the guilt offering, and of the ordinations, and of the peace offering,
7.38: which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh on Mount Sinai, on the day when He commanded the children of Yisra’ĕl to bring their offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in the Wilderness of Sinai.

8.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
8.2: “Take Aharon and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and the bull of the sin offering, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
8.3: and assemble all the congregation at the door of the Tent of Appointment.”
8.4: And Mosheh did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded him, and the congregation was assembled at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
8.5: And Mosheh said to the congregation, “This is the Word 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded to be done.”
8.6: So Mosheh brought Aharon and his sons and washed them with water,
8.7: and put the long shirt on him, and girded him with the girdle, and dressed him in the robe, and put the shoulder garment on him, and girded him with the embroidered band of the shoulder garment, and with it tied the shoulder garment on him,
8.8: and put the breastplate on him, and put the Urim and the Tummim in the breastplate,
8.9: and put the turban on his head. And on the turban, on its front, he put the golden plate, the qodesh sign of dedication, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
8.10: And Mosheh took the anointing oil and anointed the Mishkan and all that was in it, and qadosh them.
8.11: And he sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the basin and its base, to qadosh them.
8.12: And he poured some of the anointing oil on Aharon’s head and anointed him, to qadosh him.
8.13: And Mosheh brought the sons of Aharon and put long shirts on them, and girded them with girdles, and put turbans on them, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
8.14: And he brought the bull for the sin offering, and Aharon and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering,
8.15: and it was slaughtered. And Mosheh took the blood, and put some on the horns of the altar all around with his finger, and cleansed the altar. And he poured the blood at the base of the altar, and qadosh it, to make atonement for it.
8.16: And he took all the fat that was on the entrails, and the appendage on the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and Mosheh burned them on the altar.
8.17: And the bull, and its skin, and its flesh, and its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
8.18: And he brought the ram of the burnt offering, and Aharon and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram,
8.19: and it was slaughtered. And Mosheh sprinkled the blood on the altar all around,
8.20: and he cut the ram into pieces. And Mosheh burned the head, and the pieces, and the fat,
8.21: and he washed the entrails and the legs in water. And Mosheh burned the entire ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering for a sweet fragrance, and an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
8.22: And he brought the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aharon and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram,
8.23: and it was slaughtered. And Mosheh took some of its blood and put it on the tip of Aharon’s right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
8.24: And he brought near the sons of Aharon, and Mosheh put some of the blood on the tips of their right ears, and on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. And Mosheh sprinkled the blood on the altar all around,
8.25: and took the fat and the fat tail, and all the fat that was on the entrails, and the appendage on the liver, and the two kidneys and their fat, and the right thigh,
8.26: and from the basket of unleavened bread that was before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 he took one unleavened cake, and a cake of bread anointed with oil, and one thin cake, and put them on the fat and on the right thigh,
8.27: and placed all these in the hands of Aharon and in the hands of his sons, and waved them as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.28: Mosheh then took them from their hands and burned them on the altar, on the burnt offering. They were ordinations for a sweet fragrance. It was an offering by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.29: And Mosheh took the breast and waved it, a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It was Mosheh’s portion of the ram of ordination, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
8.30: And Mosheh took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood which was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aharon, on his garments, and on his sons, and on the garments of his sons with him. And he qadosh Aharon, his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons with him.
8.31: And Mosheh said to Aharon and his sons, “Cook the flesh at the door of the Tent of Appointment, and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of the ordinations, as I have commanded, saying, ‘Aharon and his sons are to eat it.’
8.32: “Then burn the rest of the flesh and the bread with fire.
8.33: “And do not go outside the door of the Tent of Appointment for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed - for He fills your hands for seven days.
8.34: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded to do, as He has done this day, to make atonement for you.
8.35: “And stay at the door of the Tent of Appointment day and night for seven days. And you shall guard the duty of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and not die, for so I have been commanded.”
8.36: And Aharon and his sons did all the words that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded by the hand of Mosheh.

9.1: And on the eighth day it came to be that Mosheh called Aharon and his sons and the elders of Yisra’ĕl.
9.2: And he said to Aharon, “Take for yourself a young bull as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering, a perfect one, and bring them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.3: “And speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Take a male goat as a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old, perfect ones, as a burnt offering,
9.4: and a bull and a ram as peace offerings, to slaughter before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall appear to you.’ ”
9.5: And they took what Mosheh commanded before the Tent of Appointment, and all the congregation drew near and stood before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.6: And Mosheh said, “This is the Word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded you to do, so that the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appears to you.”
9.7: And Mosheh said to Aharon, “Go to the altar, and prepare your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. And make the offering of the people, and make atonement for them, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded.”
9.8: So Aharon came near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself.
9.9: And the sons of Aharon brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood, and put it on the horns of the altar, and poured the blood at the base of the altar.
9.10: And the fat, and the kidneys, and the appendage on the liver of the sin offering he burned on the altar, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
9.11: And the flesh and the skin he burned with fire outside the camp.
9.12: And he slaughtered the burnt offering, and the sons of Aharon presented to him the blood, which he sprinkled on the altar all around.
9.13: And they presented the burnt offering to him, with its pieces and head, and he burned them on the altar.
9.14: And he washed the entrails and the legs, and burnt them with the burned offering on the altar.
9.15: And he brought the people’s offering, and took the goat, which was the sin offering for the people, and slaughtered it and made it a sin offering, like the first one.
9.16: And he brought the burnt offering and made it, according to the Right-Ruling.
9.17: He also brought the grain offering, and filled his hand with it, and burned it on the altar, besides the burnt offering of the morning.
9.18: And he slaughtered the bull and the ram as peace offerings, which were for the people. And Aharon’s sons presented to him the blood, which he sprinkled on the altar all around,
9.19: and the fat from the bull and the ram, the fat tail, and the covering, and the kidneys, and the appendage on the liver,
9.20: and they placed the fat on the breasts, and he burned the fat on the altar.
9.21: But the breasts and the right thigh Aharon waved as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as Mosheh had commanded.
9.22: Aharon then lifted up his hand toward the people and baraḵ them, and came down from making the sin offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
9.23: And Mosheh and Aharon went into the Tent of Appointment, and came out and baraḵ the people. And the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to all the people,
9.24: and fire came out from before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. And all the people saw and cried aloud and fell on their faces.
